sector_model: Vertical government software, SaaS transition: recurring and SaaS revenue, deferred revenue, SBC, convertible debt and buybacks; FCF after capitalized software and SBC.
thesis: Tyler Technologies (NYSE: TYL), Q3 2026 10-Q (0000860731-26-000058, filed 2026-10-28). Q3 revenue 647.6M vs 595.9M (+8.7%), 9M 1,906.2M vs 1,757.2M (+8.5%); recurring revenue 1,667.0M in 9M (87%); SaaS 695.2M. 9M operating income 311.9M vs 282.7M, NI 269.8M vs 250.1M. TTM (FY2025 + 9M26 - 9M25): revenue 2,481.3M, NI 335.3M, OCF 758.0M, PP&E capex 17.0M, capitalized software 5.8M, FCF 735.2M, SBC 158.7M (FCF after SBC 576.5M). Close 424.06 on 2026-11-13 (stockanalysis, Yahoo agree), 39,759,524 shares (cover 2026-10-26): market cap 16.86B, 50.3x TTM GAAP NI, FCF yield 4.4% (3.4% after SBC); aggregator forward P/E 28.7, EV/EBITDA 37. Balance sheet 2026-09-30: cash 788.2M plus 116.5M investments; 1,410.1M 2031 convertible notes (2026 converts of 600M repaid; capped calls 187.2M); total liabilities 2,855.1M; deferred revenue 864.3M (98% recognized within 12 months). 9M buybacks 1,124.1M cash for about 3.57M shares (about 320 average) exceeded 9M FCF of about 498M, funded by the new converts and cash; shares outstanding fell. Quality high (sticky municipal software), but price already implies steady 8 to 9% growth with margin expansion; the market view may be that AI or procurement shifts threaten vertical software, yet reported growth is steady. Not a bargain on trailing earnings.
counterthesis: 50x trailing GAAP earnings and 37x EV/EBITDA leave little margin for slower growth; growth is only 8.5% and partly acquired (9M acquisitions 239.0M, CODY and BFT; prices not read). Buybacks of 1.1B in 9M exceeded free cash flow and were funded by 1.44B converts, raising net debt to about 0.5B and diluting if converts convert; equity fell from 3.70B to 2.79B. SBC 159M TTM is 47% of net income. Government budget or federal funding cuts could slow contract wins. Remaining buyback authorization, convert terms, MD&A, peers and own history not read.
invalidation: Thesis fails if organic growth drops below about 6%, SaaS transition margins stall, buybacks continue to exceed FCF with rising leverage, or a large government customer or funding shock appears.
